title: reduce streaming token latency: token-loop, flush cadence, backpressure, and KV-cache hints
author: Priya Raman
description: Motivation: Streaming token latency had an observable tail on low-latency workloads caused by three interacting factors: the token generation loop scheduling granularity, flush cadence for partial responses, and backpressure behavior when KV-cache or batching thresholds were hit. This PR introduces a set of coordinated changes to reduce end-to-end token latency for streaming: 1) tighten the token-loop scheduling to avoid 1-2ms wakeup jitter by using a high-resolution sleep+spin policy and decoupling loop ticks from wall-clock flush intervals, 2) adaptive flush cadence: dynamically adjust partial-response flush cadence based on token arrival rate and client-side RTT heuristics to avoid unnecessary small flushes and to emit partial tokens earlier when client buffers are low, 3) improved backpressure handling: introduce a soft backpressure gate that prefers emitting partial tokens rather than stalling the stream when batching capacity is reached, and 4) KV-cache hinting: add a fast-path for KV-cache lookups during streaming where repeated prefix hits are common and avoid rebuilding small KV slices on each token. These changes are implemented with conservative defaults and feature flags (runtime.token_streaming.low_latency_mode) so we can stage rollouts. Related Linear tickets: ENG-2143 (streaming latency investigation) and ENG-2201 (kv-cache streaming optimizations). Checklist: - [x] Add token-loop scheduling changes and tests - [x] Implement adaptive flush cadence heuristic - [x] Add soft backpressure gate and unit tests - [x] KV-cache hinting fast-path and microbenchmarks - [x] End-to-end regression tests and perf benchmark updates - [x] Add feature flag and rollout plan Note: description is intentionally a single continuous string (no section breaks) per repo convention.

review_comments: Diego Alvarez: Nice work — the high-res sleep+spin reduced jitter in my local runs. Two asks: add a microbenchmark for worst-case CPU spin impact and tighten invariants around the spin fallback.
Priya Raman: Added microbenchmark and refined spin fallback. Clarified comments in token_streamer on when we switch to spin mode.
Maya Chen: Adaptive flush heuristic looks good. Suggest exposing a debug metric for 'effective_flush_interval' to track rollout impact.
Priya Raman: Added effective_flush_interval metric and dashboard tile. Fixed a corner-case where very short-lived requests could emit empty partials.
Liam O'Connor: Found a race on shutdown path where the KV hint cache could reference a freed buffer; added a fix to zero-copy slice lifetime and a test to exercise shutdown with in-flight streams.
Priya Raman: Applied Liam's patch and added integration test coverage for shutdown with streaming connections.

release_notes: Reduce streaming token latency by improving token-loop scheduling, adaptive flush cadence, soft backpressure behavior, and KV-cache streaming hints. Expected median token latency improvement: 12-18% on small-token streams; tail reduction on 99th percentile. Rollout via feature flag runtime.token_streaming.low_latency_mode; monitor streaming.latency.* metrics.
